neighbours.label: a preposition marking the target onto which something is directed or applied (light falls on, used on, pointed at, applied to), as against the same prepositions for time, place or destination
fire: At dawn the first rays of sun shine on the snowy peaks.
This cream should only be used on dry skin after washing.
The guard aimed his torch at the dark doorway.
In late afternoon the light falls on the old stone bridge.
The new filter was applied to every image in the archive.
Farmers sprayed the pesticide on the young wheat.
The officer pointed the radar gun at the speeding car.
Moonlight shone on the quiet lake for most of the night.
quiet: At dawn the first hikers arrive on the snowy peaks.
This cream should only be bought on Sundays after church.
The guard waited at the dark doorway all night.
In late afternoon we walked to the old stone bridge.
The new intern was sent to every office in the building.
Farmers met in the village hall on a Tuesday.
The officer sat in his car at the corner for hours.
The family stayed on the farm for most of the summer.

predictions: fire 0.3-0.8 on ' on', ' at', ' to' after verbs of shining, aiming, applying or using something on a target; the same prepositions for times, locations and travel destinations below 0.1
short: preposition of a target something is applied/directed onto
notes: Card: ' on' x15, ' to' x4 (applied to), ' over', ' upon', ' at' (fire a laser at), ' hits'.
